usids.rsrp_spatial_pattern: Compact deep-blue cluster (26 pixels, all >-80 dBm, 100% above excellent) enclosed by yellow boundary centered at ~33.023N, -96.703W. Signal is uniformly excellent throughout; no gradient within the boundary. Backup-mode pixels extend N and NE in teal/green (~-70 to -82 dBm). Flat southern edge of yellow boundary marks the handover limit below which no USID_00 signal reaches.

Tower NW (~33.027, -96.707). Own yellow boundary loops NW-to-center over USID_00's red-dashed area. Deep blue (excellent) fills the W/center of USID_00's boundary; NE corner has teal (~-70 dBm). Primary spatial coverage is the NW-to-center span of USID_00's footprint — the strongest and most spatially complete of the five backups.

Tower ESE (~33.022, -96.699). Own yellow boundary sits E/SE of USID_00. Deep blue covers the E/center of USID_00's red-dashed boundary; W fringe fades to teal. Provides strong complementary coverage for the right half of USID_00's footprint.

Tower S (~33.020, -96.706). Despite southward tower position, USID_41's signal propagates into the N/NW portion of USID_00's red-dashed boundary (blue block visible at ~33.027, overlapping the N edge). Own yellow boundary is well south (~33.019-33.022). The 9 absorbed pixels span the N/NW arc of USID_00's footprint.

Tower SE (~33.021, -96.700). Deep blue in the E/NE area with USID_00's red-dashed boundary on the left edge. The 7 absorbed pixels cover the E half of USID_00's zone. Yellow boundary is south of the overlap zone; a bright yellow/green band at USID_37's own peak is below and clear of USID_00's footprint.

Tower SSW (~33.019, -96.703). Own yellow boundary and blue cluster are spatially separated and well south (~33.015-33.020) of USID_00's red-dashed area. Only 2 pixels at the extreme S tip of USID_00's boundary show USID_31 signal; the rest of USID_00's footprint is grey (no signal). Minimal spatial contribution.

target_load_analysis.coverage_hole_assessment: 3 of 26 dominant pixels (11.54%) have no backup. Grey pixels are visible at the S/SW edge of the RSRP_USID_00 image, just below the flat southern portion of the yellow dominance boundary. None of the five neighbors reach this fringe — users here have no handover target for the full shutdown window.

per_backup.assessment: Primary backup absorbing 61.5% of USID_00's pixels with excellent in-zone RSRP of -57.6 dBm (100% above good). Post-outage load factor 0.013 is negligible — over 30× below the medium-risk threshold — confirming zero capacity stress.

Absorbs 42.3% of USID_00's area (E/center) with good RSRP of -58.83 dBm and mostly_mild SINR regime — backups were already competitive pre-outage in this zone. Load factor 0.011 presents no capacity concern.

Covers 34.6% of USID_00's area (N/NW) with strong RSRP of -58.5 dBm despite 4G-heavy profile (8×4G, 2×5G). Load factor 0.012 is trivial; mixed SINR regime indicates some pixels will notice USID_00's absence more than others.
Covers 26.9% of USID_00's area (E half) with good RSRP of -58.71 dBm and the lowest load factor (0.005) of all backups. Complements USID_29 for full eastern coverage with negligible load impact.

Marginal backup covering only 2 pixels (7.7%) at USID_00's S tip. In-zone RSRP is -57.54 dBm (good) and load factor 0.008 is trivial; mostly_mild regime means clean, easy handover for the two pixels it reaches.

verdict_reasoning: All five backup USIDs show post_outage_load_factor ≤ 0.013 — far below the 0.50 medium-risk threshold; zero capacity overload on any site.
100% of covered pixels achieve rsrp_pct_above_good_in_zone = 100.0% for every backup — excellent handover signal quality throughout the 88.46% covered area.
Coverage holes (11.54%, 3 pixels) are a coverage gap, not a load redistribution failure — those pixels have no backup to redistribute load to.

key_findings_for_stage3: USID_27 provides primary NW/center backup (61.5% absorption) with deep-blue excellent RSRP — the W/center half of USID_00's boundary is the strongest-covered zone.
USID_29 and USID_37 together cover the E/SE half with excellent RSRP, forming a complementary eastern corridor.
USID_41 contributes N/NW coverage (9 pixels) despite its tower being south — its beam propagates into the northern arc of USID_00's footprint.
Coverage hole (3 grey pixels = 11.54%) is confined to the S/SW fringe of USID_00's boundary — flat southern edge of yellow boundary visible in RSRP_USID_00 image marks this no-coverage zone.

reasons: All statistics sourced directly from preprocessing with zero derivation.
Image spatial claims are consistent with per_backup absorption fractions and tower positions.
Coverage hole location (S/SW edge, grey pixels) is directly visible in the RSRP_USID_00 image.
